questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: in D major, IV is G major and V is A major, a whole step apart. On that basis "G major and A major" is the supported choice. questions.explanation: All five chords are diatonic to D major: D, G, and A are major, while Bm and Em are minor. None is chromatic, so any smaller count wrongly excludes a legitimate diatonic chord.
